sections.title: The letters ur
paragraphs: The letters ur sound like the vowel in (fur) /fɜːr/, which means animal hair. This letter group makes three different sounds in English. Each sound depends on word stress or the letters that follow.

sections.title: Making the sounds
paragraphs: For the first sound, keep your tongue in the middle of your mouth. Curl the tip slightly back and make your voice hum. For the weak sound, relax your tongue completely. For the third sound, start with your tongue high, then pull it back. Touch your throat to feel your voice shake on all three.

sections.title: Spelling patterns
paragraphs: In a stressed syllable before a consonant or at the end, say (burn) /bɜːrn/. In an unstressed syllable, use the short sound heard in (sulphur) /sʌl.fər/. When a silent final e follows, say (cure) /kjʊər/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not roll your tongue like an r in Spanish or Italian. Keep your tongue steady and away from the roof of your mouth. In words like (pure) /pjʊər/, remember to add the smooth y sound before the vowel. Do not pronounce a flat u sound like the vowel in boot.
